senses.gloss:
māyīyamala
(‘the impurity of māyā’)
------------------------------------------
The various schools of शैविस्म्, have many things in common. One of them is the concept of malas or impurities. They are three: आणवमल, मायीयमल and kārmamala.
Though the पशु or the जीव (indi-vidual Self) is actually शिव in essence, he has become the very limited जीव due to his false association with the body-मिन्द् complex. This impurity of limitations is आणवमल.
Māyā is the power of शिव responsible for this च्रेअतिओन् of multiple objects, names and forms. Seeing this multiplicity, considering it as real and getting involved in it, is the मायीयमल, मल (impurity) brought about by māyā.
The मल brought about by कर्म (effect of actions of previous lives) is kārmamala.

Maya
(‘that which does not [really] exist’)
------------------------------------------
The seeds of the महाभारत war were sown at the exquisitely beautiful palace of the Pāṇḍavas in इन्द्रप्रस्थ, their capital. It was here that दुर्योधन was subject to an optical इल्लुसिओन् making himself a subject for laughter of द्रौपदी.
And, the builder of this wondrous place was मय, the chief architect of the असुरस् or demons. When अर्जुन cleared the forest Khāṇḍavavana for being consumed by अग्नि, the god of fire, मय who was living there took refuge in अर्जुन and कृष्ण who saved his life. (Mahā-bhārata, Ādiparva 228). As a token of his gratitude, मय built the palace at इन्द्रप्रस्थ (the new capital of the Pāṇḍavas). He also gave a divine गदा (mace) to भीम and the शङ्ख (conch) Devadatta to अर्जुन.
Maya was the son of कश्यप and his third wife Danu. Even from his boyhood days he was interested in the science of architecture. He acquired proficiency in it by appeasing ब्रह्मा, the creator, through severe austerities. For some time he was the king of the दानवस् (demons). Hemā was his queen. The two fierce demons, Māyāvī and दुन्दुभि, were his sons and मण्डोदरी was his daughter. She was given in मर्रिअगे to रावण of लङ्का.
‘Mayamata’ is the science of architecture attributed to him.
Viśvakarma the chief architect of the देवस् or gods was his rival in this field.
